subject: BYO key wrapping & egress segmentation review for GreenLeaf private deploy
messages:
From: Olivia Park <secops@greenleafhealth.com>

Subject: Initial BYOK & egress segmentation questions

Hi Chloe,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We reviewed the high-level BYOK proposal but the security board asked for a slightly deeper write-up specifically on two things before we move to procurement:

1) How your model of double-wrap works when we bring our own KEK (customer-managed key) but still need short-lived wrapping keys inside the private deployment. We need the sequence (who has what key material, what is persisted, how unwrapping happens during cold start).

2) Network egress segmentation: we operate under strict egress controls — any host that can unwrap data keys must be isolated and go through a bastion egress gateway that enforces TLS client certs and KMIP whitelisting. Can you confirm Redwood's recommended firewall rules and evidence for mutual-TLS enforcement?

Can you also include your recommended rotation playback testing plan (we want to validate rotations don't break replay protection or stale-cached prefixes in our runtime).

If you can send a short runbook and a diagram, that would be ideal for our next security review.

-Olivia
Security Ops, GreenLeaf Health

From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <secops@greenleafhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial BYOK & egress segmentation questions

Hi Olivia —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, attached is a compact runbook + diagram set; below is an operational summary so your board can see the safety gates. Happy to hop on a call Monday if you want to walk through the sequence.

Double-wrap model (summary):
- Customer KEK (C-KEK): customer-owned key stored in their HSM/KMS (on-prem HSM or enterprise KMS). This key never leaves customer custody.
- Local wrapping key (L-WRAP): ephemeral RSA/AES wrapping keys generated inside the private deployment's HSM-backed enclave. L-WRAP keys are short-lived (default 24h) and used to encrypt service data keys (S-DK) for local runtime use.
- Storage/transport: S-DKs are stored encrypted with L-WRAP in our encrypted secrets store inside the VPC. The L-WRAP itself is encrypted (wrapped) with the C-KEK via a KMIP or PKCS#11 operation during any persist step. Thus persistent data at rest is always wrapped with the customer KEK.
- Cold start flow: node boots -> secure enclave requests unseal token -> operator (or automated attestation flow) asks customer KMS to unwrap L-WRAP using C-KEK -> runtime then unwraps S-DK with L-WRAP.

Key custody & audit controls:
- Redwood never retains plaintext C-KEK; only wrapped blobs and audit handles are persisted.
- All unwrap operations are gated by mutual-TLS + KMIP policy and logged to the customer audit stream (syslog/S3/CloudAudit).

Rotation & playback testing (brief):
- Rotation types: scheduled KEK rotation (customer-side), rolling L-WRAP regeneration, and S-DK refresh.
- Playback test: create a pre-rotation snapshot of encrypted blobs and simulate node rebuilds against post-rotation policy to ensure unwrapping paths are valid. Runbook includes a step-by-step: 1) baseline backup, 2) rotate L-WRAP on a canary host, 3) perform read/write check, 4) validate replay protection token expiry, 5) promote rotation across pool.

Network egress segmentation (recommended):
- Only a small set of hosts (unseal proxies) should be allowed outbound to the customer KMS endpoint. These proxies live in a dedicated egress subnet and are behind a bastion egress gateway.
- Firewall (recommended iptables/SG rules):
  - Allow egress from egress-subnet to customer-KMS:443 only (destination IPs or FQDNs); deny all other egress from that subnet.
  - Host-level: block 0.0.0.0/0 outbound except to the egress gateway for application nodes.
- Mutual TLS: the egress gateway requires client certs minted by your CA; Redwood's unseal proxies present client certs, and KMS must verify. We support mTLS via PKI and KMIP client cert authentication.

Evidence & artifacts attached: diagram (redwood_byo_wrapping_diagram_v1.pdf), firewall matrix (egress_firewall_matrix.xlsx), and a rotation-playback checklist (.md).

Action items (quick):
- Olivia: confirm your KMS endpoint(s) and CA cert for mTLS so we can update the firewall matrix.
- Ben: Hannah and Ben will produce a short demo script for the playback test.

I'll follow up with the demo script and logs format.

Best,
Chloe Martin

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Initial BYOK & egress segmentation questions

Following up with specifics for the playback demo and a couple of risk notes. I'll attach a quick script (steps we ran in staging).

Playback demo steps (staging):
1) Snapshot current encrypted S-DK/L-WRAP blobs (audit-id recorded).
2) Rotate L-WRAP on canary node: generate new L-WRAP, rewrap S-DKs with new L-WRAP, persist wrapped-L-WRAP with C-KEK-wrapped header.
3) Validate: restart a canary runtime, assert it can unwrap and serve requests. Run end-to-end eval prompts to ensure KV cache prefixes are still valid for prompt continuity.
4) Playback test: restore snapshot into a sandbox with the post-rotation policy and attempt to replay historical requests that depend on older cache prefixes. Confirm system rejects stale replays and that signature-based replay-protection tokens are bound to S-DK version.

Risk notes:
- If the customer rotates C-KEK and removes old keys before Redwood has rewrapped persisted L-WRAPs, unwrapping will fail. Mitigation: require a dual-key overlap window and pre-rotation export of wrapped blobs to a recovery enclave.
- Network: DNS-based KMS endpoints are brittle if your egress rules are IP-only. Recommend allowing FQDN or keeping a narrow IP set synchronized via an approved change process.

I'll be available Monday for the demo; propose 10am PT if that works for GreenLeaf.

-Ben
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: playback-script-staging.md (inline)
